title: Ligature
description: One word in heavy geometric capitals drawn from straight stems and a single shared diagonal slope, set with ordinary loose spacing. Push it together and the letters slide in on springs; as each pair meets, their diagonals slot into one another and the shared stroke becomes a single stroke: the A's leg is the V's leg, the T's arm caps the N - each lock landing with a small settle. Let go and the word springs back open.
intent: Herb Lubalin's Avant Garde logotype and the ITC Avant Garde ligatures (https://eyemagazine.com/feature/article/up-close-and-tight): geometric capitals fitted so tight they interlock and become one shape. Make that fit the endpoint of a gesture, so loose spacing tightening into a true ligature is felt rather than shown.
